_what: the client's view of fixture v1

carried_set.derived_by: emit_schema.carried() -- the contract's own function, imported rather than re-derived (894, §23.815)

taxonomic_rung.keeps_parked: decision 886 -- server-side taxonomic aggregation is parked because the fixture already aggregates. A reader who does not know it is parked will eventually ask for per-taxon values; they are not here and that is the ruling.

node_order._what: HUC10 ids in the engine's NODE-AXIS order. Every node-lattice row is indexed by position in this list.
node_order._why_explicit: a client could infer it from the first appearance of each id in cell_keys, and that inference happens to be right today. It rests on cells being grouped by node ordinal, which nothing promises -- and a wrong node index draws the wrong river's flow, which looks entirely plausible.

cell_keys._what: cell index -> [huc10_id, band]. Every band-lattice array in this fixture is indexed by cell, and the residence layer answers in (node, band) -- this is the join between them, without which the two artefacts cannot be used together at all.
cell_keys._why_it_may_cross: a lattice reaches a client as KEYS (decisions 890, 891). This is the key structure, not a palette: it enumerates which (node, band) pairs exist, which is what residence resolves TO.

client_form.is_a_display_encoding: NOT the fixture. Values are quantised to 65,534 levels over the CONTRACT's declared bounds so a colour ramp is comparable across windows and rebuilds. Three rows in the fixture are float64 because they reach below float32's floor; that precision is deliberately not here, and anything that needs it reads fixture_v1.bin.
client_form.band_rows_quantised_node_rows_not: Band rows are quantised to 65,534 levels over the contract's bounds -- a colour ramp needs no more. Node rows are carried at full float64 because they are 1,154 wide rather than 5,684, so exactness costs ~3 MB, and because quantising streamflow over [0, 100000] would zero everything below 1.5 m3/s. HOW to render a quantity spanning that range is an open display question; this artefact does not answer it.

largest_fire/node.streamflow.not_quantised_because: the contract's bounds are [0, 100000]; 65,534 levels over that puts everything below 1.52593 at zero, and this row's smallest non-zero value is 4.941e-324

largest_fire/node.wetland_extent.not_quantised_because: the contract's bounds are [0, 1e+09]; 65,534 levels over that puts everything below 15259.3 at zero, and this row's smallest non-zero value is n/a

largest_fire.name: largest_fire
largest_fire.chosen_by: max burned_fraction_sum over water years >= 751 (the flattest quarter)
largest_fire.trend_caveat: burned_fraction_sum declines across the run, r = -0.836. A maximum over the whole post-spin-up range lands on the cutoff year rather than on a fire, so the window is chosen inside the stationary tail.
largest_fire.note: starts 1 June: the fire season, not the water year

refused_rows.node.aft.population: the aft palette has 15 members and the engine's axis is 14 wide. Any placement of one on the other is a guess, and a wrong per-life-form aggregate is indistinguishable from a right one

deepest_winter.name: deepest_winter
deepest_winter.caveat: peak SWE in this run is 9.5-32.3 mm against a 229-330 mm reference. This is the deepest winter the run HAS, not a deep winter -- see the acceptance verdict.
deepest_winter.note: starts 1 October: the water year's own start
